title: POC hosting criteria roadmap - Cobalt Assurance
summary: Intro scoping call to align POC success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks for deployment decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer has regulatory constraints (EU data residency) and bursty underwriting traffic. Agreed to 6-week pilot with mixed-hosting burst model, run Redwood micro-benchmarks + customer sample traces. Next: share SOC2 + security pack, benchmark template, cost model, and schedule kickoff lab week.

Timeline and next steps for 6-week POC

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Gomez (Redwood CSM); Alex Chen (CTO), Maya Rivera (Head of ML), Jordan Park (Infra), Priya Singh (Security), Tom Bates (Product)

Summary/Agenda: quick intros, current infra and constraints, POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, hosting tradeoffs, timeline & next steps

[00:00] Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round robin — who wants to start?
[00:07] Alex (Cobalt CTO): Alex here, I'll keep an eye on infra and exec alignment.
[00:10] Maya (Head of ML): Maya — we'll own model accuracy checks and evaluation sets.
[00:13] Jordan (Infra): Jordan — networking and security side.
[00:15] Samantha: Great. Ravi, want to run the technical framing?
[00:18] Ravi (Redwood SE): Yeah, thanks. High level, Redwood offers three hosting modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC / on-prem). For POC we usually test with a small dedicated allocation and a hosted burst path or run private if data residency/air gap is required.
[00:35] Alex: Our immediate question is around data residency — 60% of our requests originate in EU and policy says logs must stay in EU. Also underwriting peaks on mornings and month-end with bursts up to 150 qps. Baseline is about 8 qps.
[00:52] Samantha: That makes sense. For the POC, success criteria we typically track are latency SLO (p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens, and model output quality relative to your offline baseline. Anything to add, Maya?
[01:10] Maya: Yes, we need accuracy on entity extraction > 92% and hallucination rate < 3% on our validation prompt set. Also model stability over long contexts, like 2k tokens.
[01:27] Priya (Security): From security: must support customer-managed KMS for keys and audit logs with 90-day retention, and SSO (SAML) for the console. SOC2 required.
[01:40] Ravi: All standard asks. For private deployments we can do VPC-private control plane or an on-prem package for air-gapped, but that adds lead time. Dedicated gives you isolation and reserved throughput with predictable economics; hosted is fastest to start.
[02:02] Jordan: Curious about cold start and warm KV cache behavior — during bursts we saw slow tails previously. How does Redwood handle KV cache warmup across nodes?
[02:13] Ravi: Good question — we do prefix caching and pre-warm strategies; with dedicated pools you can pin a warm group to minimize coldstart. In hosted mode there's shared pools, so we recommend hybrid: dedicated baseline plus hosted overflow. That reduces cost while protecting latency.
[02:38] Tom (Product): Cost modelling — can you show rough numbers? Like for 150 qps bursts, what are we looking at for token unit costs?
[02:45] Samantha: We'll run a cost model during the benchmark sprint. Roughly, hosted per-token is higher but no infra commitment; dedicated has lower per-token with monthly commit. We'll provide a spreadsheet.
[02:58] Alex: Timeline question — we need this pilot done in 6 weeks to inform our Q3 roadmap. Is that realistic?
[03:06] Ravi: Yes — typical plan: week 0 prep (security docs, sample traces), week 1 lab kickoff and micro-benchmarks, weeks 2-4 run workload with progressive rollouts, week 5 joint analysis and tuning, week 6 decision & handoff.
[03:23] Maya: For benchmarks, what metrics do you capture? p50/p95/p99, coldstart, token cost, throughput at target latency, and accuracy diffs?
[03:30] Ravi: Exactly. We'll also measure warmup behavior, concurrency limits, GPU utilization, and p99 tail with synthetic spike tests. We'll instrument with tracing hooks.
[03:45] Priya: On compliance, we need to see an SOC2 attestation and details of data flow for hosted mode — where are logs stored, are they encrypted at rest and in transit, and cross-border transfer controls.
[03:58] Samantha: We'll send the security pack. Note that for EU residency we can provision regional hosted endpoints in eu-west, and dedicated/private can be deployed entirely in a customer's VPC in eu-west.
[04:18] Jordan: For private mode, what's the typical lead time? We're worried about network and HSM integration.
[04:25] Ravi: Private on-prem package can be 8-12 weeks depending on HSM and audit; VPC-based private control plane is closer to 3-6 weeks if there's no custom compliance gating. For the POC I'd recommend dedicated + hosted-burst to hit your 6-week timeline.
[04:46] Alex: Sounds reasonable. We also have peak jobs that send 10k token contexts — how do you handle longer contexts and memory / KV issues?
[04:56] Ravi: Our runtime supports up to 8k contexts depending on model and quantization. For long contexts we recommend model truncation policy, KV cache management and conditional caching. We'll test your 10k traces during the lab. Sometimes the transcriber here says 'K V cash' but that's KV cache — apologies for the auto-transcript issues.
[05:20] Maya: We will provide 3 representative prompt flows: underwriting short (200 tokens), audit long (6k tokens), and batch re-ranking (variable).
[05:30] Samantha: Perfect. On benchmarks we will run your traces against a small dedicated instance first, then repeat with hosted and private sim if needed. We'll measure cost per 1M tokens, latency SLO attainment, and accuracy deltas.
[05:45] Tom: On metrics, can we include business KPIs like percent of claims auto-approved and false positives?
[05:51] Maya: Yes, we'll provide a baseline dataset and conversion metrics.
[05:56] Alex: Who from your side will own the benchmarking infra?
[05:59] Samantha: Ravi will lead the bench work, Elena will coordinate POC ops and I'll own success criteria and commercial.
[06:09] Ravi: We'll also capture model regression checks — if the hosted model variance differs more than X% on your metrics we'll flag it.
[06:18] Priya: Encryption — can you support customer-managed keys in hosted?
[06:22] Ravi: Yes, we have KMS integrations for both cloud KMS (customer projects) and bring-your-own-HSM options for private.
[06:29] Jordan: Network egress — what are the flows? If we use hosted overflow, does data cross outside EU?
[06:34] Samantha: We can confine hosted overflow to EU regions; the control plane may be global but logs and inference can be regional. We'll document the flows in the security pack.
[06:46] Alex: What about SLOs for p95? We want under 300ms for short prompts and under 1s for long ones ideally.
[06:55] Ravi: That's achievable in dedicated. Hosted may hit p95 under 400ms on average depending on burst. We'll quantify in benchmarks.
[07:05] Maya: How do you handle throttling and backpressure? If our queue fills up, can Redwood return structured 429s or queue & retry?
[07:13] Ravi: We support structured 429s with Retry-After headers and can configure automatic fallback to a smaller model or cached responses. For dedicated pools we can set autoscale and burst buffers.
[07:25] Tom: Customers sometimes worry about model drift between hosted and dedicated. How deterministic are outputs?
[07:31] Ravi: Determinism depends on model and sampling parameters; we provide pinned model versions and identical model artifacts across modes to minimize drift. We'll run paired A/B checks.
[07:45] Maya: For the accuracy gate, we'll set a threshold: entity extraction F1 >= 0.92, hallucination rate < 3% and latency p95 <= 300ms for the short flows.
[07:59] Samantha: Noted. Anything else on success criteria?
[08:02] Alex: Cost per 1M tokens under a threshold — rough number TBD, but the procurement team needs a ballpark.
[08:09] Samantha: We'll include a tiered cost model in the spreadsheet for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[08:15] Elena (CSM): I'll set up a shared drive and a benchmarks tracker sheet.
[08:20] Priya: For audit logs, we need event-level logs for inference with user IDs redacted. Also a retention policy.
[08:27] Samantha: We'll include sample logs and retention options in the security pack.
[08:33] Jordan: During spikes, how do you measure GPU utilization and what tooling do you expose?
[08:38] Ravi: We can export per-instance utilization, queue depth, token/sec, and tail latency to your monitoring stack via Prometheus / Grafana or push to S3.
[08:48] Maya: Any constraints on model quantization — we use FP16 and sometimes int8. Do you have recommended quant profiles?
[08:54] Ravi: We support a few quantization paths; we'll recommend profiles based on your accuracy vs cost tradeoff after initial micro-benchmarks. The Optimize toolkit can propose quantization candidates.
[09:07] Alex: Wanted to raise procurement timing — we may need a short PO for the pilot; what's typical commercial track?
[09:13] Samantha: For pilots we do a short pilot agreement with limited spend, then convert to reserved capacity or enterprise contract afterward. We'll share commercial terms.
[09:21] Tom: On the hybrid design, can you sketch how the routing works? For instance, 90% goes to dedicated baseline, overflow to hosted with region constraints.
[09:29] Ravi: Yes, routing policies can target by latency tolerance, model variant, region, or cost. You can set a policy: route to dedicated pool while utilization < 70%, overflow to eu-hosted endpoints, and fallback to a cheaper quantized model if p95 rises. We'll provide a sample policy.
[09:49] Alex: That should cover the operational needs. Let's talk timeline concretely.
[09:52] Samantha: Week 0 (this week) — exchange security docs and traces. Week 1 — lab kickoff with Redwood bench team. Week 2-3 — run throughput and spike tests. Week 4 — accuracy and regression checks; Week 5 — tuning and cost modeling; Week 6 — decision meeting and recommendations.
[10:09] Maya: One question: can we run synthetic 10k token long-context tests safely without exposing PII?
[10:14] Priya: We'll sanitize; Maya will produce synthetic variants.
[10:17] Samantha: Great. Any blockers we should note?
[10:20] Jordan: Need clarification on VPC peering IP ranges and whether we need dedicated NAT for logs.
[10:25] Samantha: We'll include network checklist in the runbook.
[10:28] Alex: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[10:30] Samantha: Recap — Redwood sends security pack and benchmark template; customer sends traces and OKR approval; schedule kickoff week of 2026-05-25.
[10:40] Elena: I'll send calendar invites and create the tracker.
[10:42] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[10:44] Samantha: Thanks, we'll follow up with the attachments.

Notes: transcript has occasional mislabels and auto-transcribe artifacts (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache). The meeting included an AE+SE pair and covered hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, hybrid burst design, EU residency, KMS, SOC2, benchmarks and a 6-week pilot timeline.

End of transcript.
